title: Connectors
description: data/connectors.json, schema 2.1 -- every connector (Verbindungsmittel) of the project, in file-name order, built by calc/domains/connector.py from the sources Woodcore writes (docs/domain/connectors.md §7bis, §3.3nonies). Until 2.0 a connector was a row of Positionen.xlsx's Positions Connectors sheet and descriptive only; it is now a file of its own and carries its own calculation. The descriptive half kept every key it had, under the same names and types, so that show-connector and the reference workbook did not have to change for the move. Generated, never hand-edited.

schema_version.description: -- pinned: an export written at another version is refused rather than read as this one. 3.0 is the move to a detail schema: the geometry is named rather than carried, so `schema` replaces `reference`/`orientation`, a fastener carries the marker's id beside its place, and a member names an element instead of a section (v0.74). 2.1 added the identity's `name` and `variant` and the connection's one `moisture_class` with its `moisture_from`; 2.0 carried a moisture class per member. 3.1 (issue #42): a record may carry `links`.

position.description: The connector's id: its file name, connectors/<id>.json.

type.description: The kind of fastener, one of connector.TYPES (Stabdübel, Vollgewindeschraube, ...).

assembly.description: The kind of assembly, one of dowel.ASSEMBLIES or dowel.UNCOVERED_ASSEMBLIES (Holz-Holz zweischnittig, ...).

diameter.description: The diameter, {value, unit} in mm, or null where the sheet leaves it empty.

length.description: The length, {value, unit} in mm, or null.

dimension.description: Any other dimension, as typed -- descriptive text, never parsed; may be empty.

steel.description: The grade of a Stahl-Holz joint's plates, from SIA 263 Tabelle 1 (calc/norms/sia263-2013-tab01-baustaehle.json), or empty.

predrilled.description: Ja (true), Nein (false), or null where the sheet leaves it empty.

elements.description: The ids of the Positions Element rows the connector joins, in the order typed.

group.description: The folder Woodcore files this connector in, "" at the root -- the source's own field, carried here so that a reader need not open the source (calc/tools/grouped_list.py). Optional and additive, so the export's schema_version is deliberately not bumped for it.

label.description: What the engineer calls this connector; may be empty.

name.description: What the engineer calls this connector; with `variant` it is what the default id was composed of.

variant.description: Which variant of that name this is; may be empty.

source.description: The source file this was built from, connectors/<id>.json.

calculated.description: false where the type has no calculation module yet, or where a member's timber did not resolve. The descriptive half is complete either way; the report refuses to print a resistance nobody produced and says `reason` instead.

reason.description: Why `calculated` is false; empty when it is true.

conditions.description: What the engineer stated about the connection: seismic (eta_t = 1.4, SIA 265 2.2.6) and truss (the 0.75 of 5.3.6.2.2, given as a second result).

moisture_class.description: The connection's Feuchteklasse, 1, 2 or 3 -- ONE per connection, which is what eta_w is read with (SIA 265 Tabelle 4). null where neither the source nor the members' positions give one, which is a reason `calculated` is false.

moisture_from.description: Where that class came from, in words: «Feuchteklasse 2, aus Position T001» or «..., im Verbindungsmittel festgelegt (Positionen: T001 -> 2)». What Woodcore prints in orange under an overridden field, and what the report can print beside eta_w.

n_tot.description: The total number of fasteners the resistance was calculated with.

n_tot_override.description: true where the engineer set n_tot by hand instead of taking the drawing's own count. The export carries a warning and the report prints it.

fasteners.description: The fasteners this connector carries: the schema's marker id and the place that marker sits at, in the order the source ticked them. The coordinates are the schema's own frame -- mm, x right, z down -- so a polar-moment calculation drawn on the same schema reads the same numbers with no conversion. A marker the schema no longer carries is left out, with a warning.

members.description: The members meeting at the node: their drawing fields, and for a timber member the resolved strength class, density, species, moisture class and the thickness, angle and fastener row the calculation read -- each with where it came from.

element.description: The id of the schema element this member is; "" for one that names none yet. The element's direction is the member's grain and its `position` is the row of Positions Element the strength class and the moisture class are read from.

position.description: The position the member's element names, resolved here so a reader need not open the schema; "" where the element names none or the schema no longer carries it.

grade.description: The resolved strength class, or empty.

species.description: Nadelholz or Laubholz, read off the strength class.

material_from.description: Where the strength class came from: «GL24h, aus Position T001» or «GL24h, im Verbindungsmittel festgelegt». The reference is resolved afresh at every export, so this records what it resolved to.

results.description: The vars this calculation ends on -- R_d_Verb and R_d, and R_d_Verb_Fachwerk where the connection is a truss node. Empty where `calculated` is false.

tables.description: The tabular evidence, each with the level and the side it belongs on.

steps.description: Its steps, in the order it is carried out.

checks.description: Always empty. There is no design force here: the report states F_d and the verification itself, with #verify reading var-of("connector", id, "R_d").

warnings.description: What the export could not keep quiet about and the report prints beside the calculation: a fastener count set by hand, a distance below SIA 265 Tabelle 24, a k_beta equation applied outside the thicknesses it is stated for.

figures.description: The drawings, by kind ('pattern', 'section') and then by language -- one file per language, as a connection's are, because a frame is sized from its own text (docs/typst/language.md §4bis). Absent while the export draws none.

section_scaled.description: What the section figure had to resize: "enlarged" or "reduced" where the diameter is drawn at a bound rather than to scale, else empty. The figure carries no word, so the report writes the note under it in its own language (glossary engine keys connector.section_enlarged / connector.section_reduced).

schema.description: The detail schema this connector is drawn on -- a file of details/, whose elements are its members and whose connector markers carry its fasteners (docs/domain/detail-schemas.md §3.3decies). Empty for one that names none yet, which `calculated` then says could not be calculated.

links.description: Where each field that follows a variable came from (REQ-012): the entry ("self", an id, or `collection[i]`), the field, the variable, the factor and offset it was taken with, its own value and unit, and `stale` where it could not be read and the source's last value was used. Absent where none follows one.

variable.description: A variable of the export this field follows (calc/domains/links.py, spec 2026-10-11-variables-liees-champs-et-textes D-17): the pair a call names its calculation by and its key -- a domain of the «Formule» tab carries origin "formulas" and its id as instance --, with an optional factor and offset (factor × variable + offset).
